name: Zero-knowledge file encryptor & self-decrypting envelope
description: When sharing sensitive financial statements, tax filings, legal contracts, or confidential identity documents, traditional cloud file-sharing services store your data unencrypted on their servers or hold the master decryption keys. PrivacyFold's Zero-Knowledge File Encryptor implements military-grade AES-256-GCM symmetric encryption combined with PBKDF2 key derivation using 600,000 SHA-256 iterations directly inside your browser via the W3C Web Cryptography API. Rather than requiring recipients to install proprietary decryption software, the tool packages your encrypted payload into a self-decrypting HTML envelope. Any recipient with the correct passphrase can open the HTML file in any modern web browser on Windows, macOS, Linux, iOS, or Android, enter the password, and decrypt the original file with zero software installations and zero network requests.

seo.metaTitle: Encrypt Files into Self-Decrypting HTML Envelopes (AES-256-GCM) | PrivacyFold
seo.metaDescription: Encrypt any file locally using AES-256-GCM and PBKDF2. Generates self-decrypting HTML envelopes that open offline in any browser. 100% zero-knowledge.
seo.aeoSummary: PrivacyFold's Zero-Knowledge File Encryptor uses native WebCrypto AES-256-GCM and 600,000-iteration PBKDF2 to seal files into portable self-decrypting HTML packages. Encryption and decryption occur entirely offline without transmitting passphrases or ciphertext to any server.

faqs.question: How does the recipient decrypt the file if they do not have PrivacyFold installed?
faqs.answer: The output is a standard HTML document containing the encrypted ciphertext and a minimal offline WebCrypto decryption script. The recipient simply double-clicks the HTML file in any browser (Chrome, Safari, Edge, Firefox), types the password, and the browser decrypts and saves the original file to their device.

faqs.question: Can PrivacyFold or any government agency recover my file if I lose my password?
faqs.answer: No. This is a true zero-knowledge cryptographic implementation. Your passphrase never leaves your device's volatile memory, and we possess no master keys or backdoors. If you lose your password, the ciphertext is mathematically unrecoverable.

faqs.question: Why is AES-256-GCM with PBKDF2 considered the gold standard for file security?
faqs.answer: AES-256-GCM provides both strong confidentiality and cryptographic authenticity (tamper-proofing). If anyone attempts to alter even a single bit of the encrypted file, decryption fails with an authentication error. PBKDF2 with 600,000 iterations protects against brute-force and GPU dictionary attacks.

faqs.question: Does the self-decrypting HTML file connect to the internet to decrypt?
faqs.answer: No. The self-decrypting HTML file contains 100% self-contained vanilla JavaScript that uses the recipient browser's native window.crypto.subtle engine. It functions flawlessly with airplane mode enabled and network cables disconnected.

faqs.question: What is the maximum file size I can encrypt into a self-decrypting envelope?
faqs.answer: Most modern browsers comfortably handle files up to 250 MB into an HTML envelope. For files larger than 500 MB, we recommend dedicated offline archives.

faqs.question: Can I encrypt multiple files into a single encrypted envelope?
faqs.answer: Yes. You can bundle multiple files into a single zip archive and encrypt the resulting zip file into the HTML envelope.

steps: Select or drag the sensitive document, spreadsheet, PDF, or image you wish to protect.
Enter a strong passphrase or generate a cryptographically random 128-bit key.
The WebCrypto engine generates a unique 96-bit cryptographic initialization vector (IV) and 128-bit salt.
Your file is encrypted in memory with authenticated AES-GCM, producing ciphertext with an integrity authentication tag.
Download the resulting self-decrypting HTML file and share it securely via email, USB drive, or messaging apps.

settingsExplained.name: Passphrase Strength
settingsExplained.description: Input password used to derive the 256-bit AES master key via PBKDF2. Longer passphrases drastically increase resistance to dictionary attacks.
settingsExplained.example: Use 4 random words (e.g. "correct-horse-battery-staple") for optimal security.

settingsExplained.name: PBKDF2 Iteration Count
settingsExplained.description: Determines the computational work required to test passwords. PrivacyFold enforces 600,000 iterations per OWASP 2026 security benchmarks.
settingsExplained.example: Makes brute-force dictionary cracking infeasible even on high-end GPUs.

settingsExplained.name: Envelope Title & Notes
settingsExplained.description: Optional unencrypted title displayed on the decryption screen to guide the recipient without revealing confidential file details.
settingsExplained.example: "Q4 Board Financials — Enter agreed boardroom passphrase".

whatToExpect.results: A self-contained .html file containing base64-encoded AES-256-GCM ciphertext, 12-byte IV, 16-byte salt, and an inline clean decryption portal.
whatToExpect.limits: Supports files up to 250 MB per envelope. Encryption speed averages 40 MB/second in modern WebCrypto implementations.
whatToExpect.benchmarks: 600,000 PBKDF2 iterations execute in ~120ms on Apple Silicon and modern Intel/AMD processors.

privacyProof.howItWorks: Uses window.crypto.subtle.deriveKey() with PBKDF2 and window.crypto.subtle.encrypt() with AES-GCM. No external cryptographic libraries are imported.
verificationSteps: Encrypt a test document with a passphrase.
Open the generated HTML envelope in a new private browser tab with Wi-Fi disabled: verify full offline decryption capability.
privacyProof.openSourceNotice: Auditable, zero-dependency implementation conforming to W3C Web Cryptography API and NIST SP 800-38D.
